item: Whole organisation or a defined, separately managed sub-set; end-user devices must be in scope
repo_note: Scoping decision for the organisation; repo does not define certification scope.

item: Every cloud service holding org data (IaaS/PaaS/SaaS) is in scope and cannot be excluded
repo_note: IaC lists deployed resources; no inventory of CI host, identity, stores, monitoring SaaS accounts.

item: Per cloud service, confirm which controls the provider implements, backed by contract or trust-centre statements
repo_note: No rule to record shared-responsibility split per provider; an ADR would fit (20 §2).

item: BYOD and home/remote devices accessing org data/services are in scope; ISP routers out, so device firewalls apply
repo_note: Workforce device policy; repo is silent on developer laptops beyond 14 §1 local stack.

item: Accounts used by third parties, MSPs and contractors are in scope and must meet the controls
repo_note: Machine identities federated and scoped; human third-party/contractor accounts not addressed.

item: Commercial web apps in scope; bespoke app components out of scope; follow Software Security Code of Practice
repo_note: Product code is bespoke so out of CE scope; SDLC rules align but no SSCoP mapping.

item: Asset management (recommended, not a control): authoritative, maintained asset information
repo_note: IaC and deletion lists inventory cloud resources; no device or software-on-device inventory.

item: Backups recommended (not a requirement); turn on automatic backups
repo_note: Deletion protection and per-customer backups; PITR optional (paid); no restore-test rule.

item: Every in-scope device and cloud service protected by a correctly configured firewall or data-flow policy
repo_note: Edge firewall and origin access control for cloud; laptops and self-hosted runners not addressed.

item: Default firewall/admin passwords changed to strong unique ones, or remote admin disabled
repo_note: No rule on cloud root account, device or router admin credentials.

item: Admin interface not internet-reachable unless documented need plus MFA or IP allow list
repo_note: Changes go via pipeline; cloud console remains internet-facing with no MFA or allow-list rule.

item: Unauthenticated inbound connections blocked by default
repo_note: Gateway refuses tokenless requests; anonymous endpoints explicit; buckets private behind origin access.

item: Inbound rules approved and documented by an authorised person with the business need
repo_note: Rules are IaC, reviewed as a plan in a PR; guard tests pin scanner rules.

item: Unnecessary firewall rules removed or disabled when no longer needed
repo_note: Rule budget forces pruning; no periodic rule-review requirement.

item: Software firewall on devices used on untrusted networks (home, public wifi)
repo_note: Endpoint configuration for staff devices; not in repo.

item: Remove or disable unnecessary user accounts (guest, unused admin)
repo_note: No open sign-up, role split; nothing on pruning unused cloud/CI/store accounts.

item: Change default or guessable account passwords
repo_note: App stores no passwords and sets length policy; devices and vendor consoles not covered.

item: Remove or disable unnecessary software, utilities and network services
repo_note: Strong for app dependencies and exposed endpoints; nothing for runner or laptop software.

item: Disable auto-run that executes files without user authorisation
repo_note: Package install scripts off everywhere (analogue); OS auto-run on devices not addressed.

item: Users authenticated before access to org data or services
repo_note: Managed identity; token verified at edge and gateway before any code.

item: Device unlock credential; throttle or lock after 10 attempts; PIN at least 6 characters
repo_note: Device/MDM policy; mobile app only keeps tokens in platform secure storage.

item: Cloud services (IaaS/PaaS/SaaS) configured securely, not left at defaults
repo_note: Public access blocked, TLS minimum, encryption, retention; guard tests keep settings on.

item: All in-scope software licensed and supported, vendor end-of-support date known
repo_note: Package vetting checks maintainers, not support status; no runtime or OS end-of-life tracking.

item: Unsupported software removed, or isolated in a sub-set with no internet traffic
repo_note: No rule to retire end-of-life runtimes, base images, OS on runners.

item: Automatic updates enabled where possible
repo_note: Dependency updater weekly, 7-day cooldown; devices and runners not covered.

item: Critical/high (CVSS v3 7+) or unrated fixes applied within 14 days of release
repo_note: Only newly added advisories fail; existing ones listed with no deadline; cooldown eats 7 of 14 days.

item: Patching covers servers, IaaS images, firewalls/routers, and self-hosted runner OS
repo_note: Digest-pinned images freeze patches; runner provisioning doc has no patch rule.

item: Laptops, tablets and phones (incl. BYOD) kept updated
repo_note: Workforce device management; not in repo.

item: A process to create and approve user accounts
repo_note: Admin-only creation with single-use link for app users; no process for staff cloud/CI accounts.

item: Unique credentials per user before access to applications or devices
repo_note: Per-user app identity and per-run pipeline creds; shared human console accounts not banned.

item: Remove or disable accounts no longer required (leavers, inactivity period)
repo_note: Suspension exists for customers; no leaver or inactivity rule for any account.

item: MFA wherever available; cloud services must always use MFA (auto-fail since Apr 2026)
repo_note: TOTP offered in app, not mandated; nothing for cloud console, git/CI host, stores, registries.

item: Separate accounts used only for administrative activity
repo_note: Role split for operators and read-only plan role; no separate human admin accounts rule.

item: Remove special privileges when no longer required (role change)
repo_note: Least privilege at design time for deployables; no access review or revocation trigger.

item: Accounts grant only the access the role needs
repo_note: Role gate, ownership, field filtering; per-deployable roles naming exact resources.

item: Password brute-force protection: MFA, or throttle (10 per 5 min), or lockout after 10
repo_note: Managed identity and rate limits; no explicit throttle or lockout setting required.

item: Password quality: MFA, or 12+ characters, or 8+ with deny list; no maximum length
repo_note: Length-based policy stated, but no minimum number, deny list or max-length rule.

item: No forced expiry or complexity rules; support password managers and unique passwords
repo_note: Rejects character-class rules; silent on expiry and user guidance.

item: Passwordless (passkeys/FIDO2) as preferred default
repo_note: No passkey or FIDO2 rule anywhere.

item: Process to change passwords promptly when compromise is known or suspected
repo_note: Documented rotation for secrets; no user or staff credential compromise procedure.

item: Malware protection active on every in-scope laptop/desktop/phone (anti-malware or allow listing)
repo_note: Workforce endpoint control; not in repo.

item: Self-hosted CI/build runners have active malware protection
repo_note: Runner hygiene cleans secrets and caches; no anti-malware or allow-list requirement.

item: Application allow listing: only approved, code-signed applications run; current approved list
repo_note: Supply-chain analogue (approval, SHA/digest/hash pins); not device application allow listing.

item: Cloud/PaaS malware protection confirmed with provider; uploaded content controlled
repo_note: Uploads type- and size-pinned via signed URL; no malware scan of uploads.

item: TC1 external vulnerability scan of all internet-facing IPs/services
repo_note: Hardened edge helps pass; no rule to run external scans.

item: TC2 authenticated scan of sampled devices/servers/IaaS: no CVSS 7+ fix older than 14 days
repo_note: No device or runner scanning; dependency audit only.

item: TC3 malware tests via email attachments and browser downloads on sampled devices
repo_note: Workforce endpoint and mail filtering; not in repo.

item: TC4 assessor observes MFA on each cloud service for normal and admin users
repo_note: Would fail today: no MFA mandate for staff cloud accounts.

item: TC5 account separation: standard user cannot run admin processes without admin credentials
repo_note: Endpoint local-admin policy; not in repo.

item: Scope and sub-set segregation verified technically; any single failed sub-test fails the assessment
repo_note: Separate cloud accounts per environment support segregation evidence.
